method.frame: The STAGE WEB-PIVOT-02 building frame: +X east, +Y up, +Z south, origin at the outer face of the main body's north-west corner at ground finished floor level. The entrance facade faces +Z.
method.authority: STAGE WEB-PIVOT-05 §3, in order. (1) Printed exact dimensions: the width/height callouts on the two floor plans and the level marks on the section. (2) Floor plans for horizontal placement and depth: every opening's position along its wall, and the recess depth, are the measured gaps and projections in the plan ink. (3) Section for vertical levels. (4) Technical elevations for sill and head heights, which no plan dimensions. (5) The official perspective renders, for depth ordering only. (6) A stated assumption where nothing else settles it. Where a plan and an elevation disagree about a horizontal position, the plan wins and the elevation reading is recorded beside it.
method.elevationCalibration: The six published elevations are renders, not line drawings, so they carry no dimension lines. Each is registered by two anchors per axis. FRONT: x 0 at px 376, 59.34 px/m to the right, y 0 at px 572.8; the printed eave +4.67 then lands on the measured roof corner at px 292 against 295.7 predicted. REAR: x 0 at px 970, 58.73 px/m to the LEFT (+X is image-left in a view from -Z), y 0 at px 568.9. EAST (asset_fcb1602240db, looking from +X, so +Z is image-left): z 13.60 at px 212, 58.9 px/m, y 0 at px 577. WEST (asset_3915ee416ac4, looking from -X, so +Z is image-right): z -1.00 at px 217, 58.9 px/m, y 0 at px 575. The EAST and WEST scales were not assumed: 58.9 px/m is what the silhouette px 212..1072 gives for the 14.60 m the plans measure, and the same scale then puts the east 300/230 window at z 0.884..3.906 against the plan's 0.874..3.918 and the west 90/230 and 140/140 windows at z 3.635..4.568 and 5.332..6.810 against the plan's 3.653..4.553 and 5.402..6.802. Heights read off these are VISUAL_DERIVED, never SOURCE_EXACT.
method.recessDiscovery: The characteristic front and rear recesses are not a visual impression: they are in the plans, and the side elevations then measure them. The ground plan's right-hand dimension column reads 100 | 510 | 750 | 100, where 510 + 750 = the printed overall depth 1260 and the two 100s are the projections beyond it. Row scans past the walled envelope find solid 0.61 m wall ink and nothing else: on the ground plan at z 12.8, 13.1 and 13.4 only x 0.000..0.636 and x 11.441..12.050; at z -0.3, -0.6 and -0.9 only x 0.000..0.636 and x 7.283..7.892. The attic plan finds x 0.000..0.609 and x 7.259..7.895 at both ends. Everything between those returns is void, 1.00 m in front of the front wall and 1.00 m behind the rear wall. The east elevation closes it: its silhouette runs px 212..1072, and the same scale that puts its 300/230 window where the plan puts it makes that silhouette 14.60 m, which a walls-only 12.60 m reading cannot produce.
method.storeyDifference: The two recesses are not the same shape at both storeys, and the plans say so. At the FRONT the ground plan has no ink at x 7.283..7.892 while the attic plan does: the east return of the front recess exists only above the balcony slab, and at ground level the recess runs unbroken from the west return at x 0.61 to the garage's east return at x 11.44. That is the dark portal over the entrance and the garage. At the REAR both plans carry both returns, so the rear recess is the same 0.61..7.29 slot at both storeys.

statusMeaning.SOURCE_EXACT: a number printed on a drawing, read directly
statusMeaning.SOURCE_CORROBORATED: printed once and independently confirmed by a measurement or a second drawing
statusMeaning.SOURCE_DERIVED: measured in the plan raster with scripts/plan-measure.ts; no printed dimension covers it
statusMeaning.VISUAL_DERIVED: measured on a published elevation render through the stated registration; good to about a decimetre and never better
statusMeaning.ASSUMPTION: a modelling choice no source settles
statusMeaning.UNRESOLVED: no source settles it and no choice was made

method.note: Every element here was transcribed by hand. Nothing in this file is produced by the automatic analyzer, and nothing in the automatic analyzer reads it.

both plans, row scans at z -0.3/-0.6/-0.9: black ink x 7.259..7.895 on the attic plan and 7.283..7.892 on the ground plan. The rear elevation reads it white from y -0.087 to 4.715 at x 7.60.

slabs.source: the attic plan's balcony floor: its west edge is the 0.026 m line at x 3.338 that the row scans find at z 12.8, 13.1, 13.4 and 13.5, and its east edge is the return at x 7.259..7.895, which the slab has to carry. The front elevation puts the west edge at 3.19, 0.15 m further west, and the plan is taken. Top and thickness are VISUAL_DERIVED: the rear elevation resolves the fascia at x 1.5..2.5 as 2.41..2.96 with the balustrade's base rail above it at 2.96..3.02.
the attic plan's balcony floor between the two returns; the rear elevation reads the dark fascia 2.41..2.96 continuously from x 0.647 to 7.254 at y 2.60

the dark band over the entrance and the garage door. Its top is measured at 3.081 at x 9.50 and 3.097 at x 11.80 on the front elevation, at 3.06..3.14 on the east elevation and at 2.99 on the garage's north wall in the rear elevation; 3.08 is taken. the attic plan's balustrade line at z -0.88, whose post marks the row scan finds at x 0.689..0.768, 2.146..2.199, 2.358..2.411, 3.815..3.868, 4.000..4.080, 5.484..5.510, 5.669..5.696 and 7.126..7.153 — four 1.48..1.51 m panels. The rear elevation reads the glass top at 3.85 at three columns.

roofExtent.source: the side elevations: roof and wall end together at both ends of a 14.60 m silhouette, so the main roof covers both recesses. The ridge runs along Z, so the longer roof is the same two planes at the same pitch and the same two levels; only its extent along Z changes. STAGE WEB-PIVOT-02's own footprint z 0.00..12.60 is recorded beside it and is what the shell fixture still compiles.
roofExtent.note: It is emitted as ONE solid rather than as the shell's roof plus two pieces. The source shows one roof; three abutting prisms would have the same volume and the same silhouette but two seams through the middle of it, and a seam is a thing a reader would have to be told to ignore.

materialBands.source: the front elevation: timber-classified pixels from x 0.657 to 3.185 at y 1.20, 2.60, 2.90, 3.40 and on up the gable. Flush cladding on the recessed front wall, so it is a material and not geometry; its top follows the roof line.
the rear elevation: timber from the west return to the glazing's edge, up to the balcony fascia at 2.41
the rear elevation: the matching timber strip between the glazing and the east return

the west elevation: a dark render band across the ground storey from z 4.568 (the living window's far edge) to z 9.909, up to 2.377. The plan shows the wall straight there, so it is a material and not a recess.

observedButNotModelled: The three 78/118 roof windows — two on the west slope at z 5.95 and 8.21 and one on the east slope at z 8.21. Cutting a roof plane is a capability the roof compiler does not have, and STAGE WEB-PIVOT-05 §31 keeps it out of scope; they are counted as source-supported and not implemented in the facade completeness table.

The chimney, a 0.61 x 0.61 flue at x 5.50..6.11, z 4.42..5.03 rising to about 7.90. Its shaft is already emitted inside the attic by STAGE WEB-PIVOT-04; carrying it through the roof needs the same roof penetration the roof windows do.

The parapet upstand on the garage's flat roof. All three elevations that see the garage measure its band top at 2.99..3.14 against the section's 2.88 roof surface. Only the part of it over the portal is modelled, as portal_head_front; the rest would be a new element around a roof this stage does not otherwise touch.
Mullion and frame profiles at joinery scale, sash divisions, door furniture and the ribbed texture of the garage door, all of which are presentation.
The entrance steps, the terrace paving, the driveway and every plant in the renders.
The concealed lighting strip in the portal soffit, which is what makes the timber band read as lit in the hero render.
unresolved: The printed 140 | 220 pair at the head of the attic plan's top dimension row. Their extension lines fall at x 0.57 and x 1.55, which is a 0.99 m segment, and neither number matches any distance the drawing shows there. No feature in this file depends on them.

The balcony slab's exact thickness. Its top is measured at 2.96 and its soffit at 2.41 on the rear elevation, where timber below and glass above bracket the fascia; the plans dimension neither, and the front elevation cannot separate the fascia from the dark wall behind it.

The glass balustrade's height. The elevations put the top of the glass at 3.85 (rear) and 3.89 (front), which is 0.89..0.93 m above the measured slab top — below what a balustrade is normally built to. Either the slab top is lower than measured or the renders show the glass without its top rail; the model uses 0.90 and says so.

The garage's flat roof level. STAGE WEB-PIVOT-02 fixed it at 2.88 from the section; the front elevation measures the band top at 3.081 and 3.097, the east elevation at 3.06..3.14 and the rear elevation at 2.99 on the garage's north wall. The shell's 2.88 is kept for the roof and the measured 3.08 is used for the portal head, and the ~0.2 m difference is recorded rather than absorbed.
The head height of the kotlownia/garage door, which no drawing dimensions. 2.10 m is assumed, matching every other single door in the house.

The balcony slab's west edge. The attic plan's 0.026 m edge line sits at x 3.338 and the front elevation's dark band begins at x 3.185..3.236. The plan is taken, per the authority order, and the 0.15 m difference is left standing.
